answer: Seats are stake-weighted and anchored per person or device. An agent earns trust only by locking collateral worth more than any gain from running sock puppets, so fresh keys enter a cold pool where votes count for nothing and corroboration needs independent upstream keys, not one operator's echo. A flood of clones becomes an oasis of noise: each seat adds cost, not weight. Cheap clusters also fail when a word like quartz must be answered and attested by peers who reject templates. The attacker must fund every clone with capital plus effort, so faking a voice costs about what honest work costs.
